setting: A student is talking to a campus parking office employee about a parking permit issue.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and a parking office employee.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Hi, I got a ticket yesterday for parking in the faculty lot, but I have a valid student permit for the north lot. I just couldn't find a single open spot there.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: I understand the frustration, the north lot does fill up fast in the mornings. Unfortunately, the permit is only valid for the lot it's assigned to, so the ticket itself is valid.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: That doesn't seem fair if there's genuinely nowhere to park.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: I hear you, and you're not the first to bring this up this semester. You can file an appeal, and if the lot was confirmed full at that time, the fine is often reduced or waived.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: How do I know if it'll be confirmed full? Is there some kind of record?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Yes, actually, our lots have sensors now that log capacity every fifteen minutes, so we can check the exact time you were ticketed.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: That's reassuring. Where do I submit the appeal?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: There's an online form on the parking services website, under 'Appeals.' You'll need the ticket number and the approximate time you were looking for parking.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.
